lines.text: Viking Age wives wore their husbands' savings.
In 921, Ibn Fadlan left Baghdad with an embassy to the Volga.
lines.say: In nine twenty one, Ibn Fadlan left Baghdad with an embassy to the Volga.

lines.text: There he met traders called the Rus and noted what they wore.
Each wife wore a small metal box on her chest.
The metal ranged from iron to gold, by her husband's wealth.
Her neck wore gold and silver bands, one per 10,000 dirhams.
lines.say: Her neck wore gold and silver bands, one per ten thousand dirhams.

scene.label: A Viking neck ring, the Walters

lines.text: A rich wife could wear many bands at once.
Their most prized jewelry was green beads, a dirham for each.
A wife wearing three bands meant her husband had 30,000 dirhams.
lines.say: A wife wearing three bands meant her husband had thirty thousand dirhams.

post.caption: Viking Age wives wore their husbands' savings. In 921, Ibn Fadlan left Baghdad with an embassy to the Volga. There he met traders called the Rus and noted what they wore. Each wife wore a small metal box on her chest. The metal ranged from iron to gold, by her husband's wealth. Her neck wore gold and silver bands, one per 10,000 dirhams. A rich wife could wear many bands at once. Their most prized jewelry was green beads, a dirham for each. A wife wearing three bands meant her husband had 30,000 dirhams.
